test_title: PYST 1: SSC Stenographer - English (Held On:12 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

He said, “I am living in Ludhiana.”

options.text: He said that he was living in Ludhiana.
He said that he is living in Ludhiana.
He said that he has been living in Ludhiana.
He asked that he is living in Ludhiana.

solution:
The correct answer is '**He said that he was living in Ludhiana**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting direct speech to reported speech, the tense usually shifts back one step. In this case, the present continuous "**am living**" becomes the past continuous "**was living**".
 
• The pronoun also changes to maintain the perspective. Thus "**I**" changes to "**he**" to match the subject in the reported speech.
 
• In reported speech, the structure of the sentence often requires the conjunction "**that**" to introduce the reported clause, though it can be omitted in informal speech.
 
• The verb "**said**" is used for statements. Other verbs like "**asked**" are used for questions or requests, which is not the case here.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is '**He said that he was living in Ludhiana.**'

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2, "**He said that he is living in Ludhiana,**" does not correctly shift the tense from present continuous to past continuous, which is typically required in reported speech.
 
• Option 3, "**He said that he has been living in Ludhiana,**" changes the verb tense to present perfect continuous, which alters the original meaning conveyed in direct speech.
 
• Option 4, "**He asked that he is living in Ludhiana,**" incorrectly uses "asked," which should be used for questions or requests, not statements. Additionally, it does not shift the tense to past.
